kurz: When whisked, proteins unfold and form a skin around air bubbles. That creates a stable foam.
bild_im_kopf: Like soap bubbles whose skin is made of protein instead of soap.
was_passiert: The whisk beats air into the [[eiweiss|egg white]] and stretches the protein [[molekuel|molecules]]. They settle around the air bubbles and link into a skin. Fat disrupts this skin, which is why no yolk must get in. A little acid and gradually added sugar make the foam more stable.
warum_wichtig: [[g-meringue|Meringue]], sponge, mousse and soufflé get their air from this foam, without any baking powder.
faustregeln: A pinch of acid or [[weinstein|cream of tartar]] stabilises.
Sprinkle in sugar only once soft peaks form.
Egg whites at room temperature whip up better.

stellschrauben.wirkung: whisk longer → stiffer, too long → grainy

praxis.text: Egg whites for sponge and soufflé: stiff but still glossy.
Cream forms a foam through its fat: whip it well chilled, otherwise it turns to butter.
A sponge rises only through the whipped-in air, so fold gently.
